title: db: SQLAlchemy models + session
test_cmd: uv run python -c "from realm.db.models import Base, World, Player, BotProfile, Tile, Village, Building, BuildQueue, Troop, TrainingQueue, Movement, Event, Report; print(sorted(Base.metadata.tables))"
criteria: realm/db/models.py defines a DeclarativeBase named `Base` and exactly these 12 classes with SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed `Mapped[]` columns: World, Player, BotProfile, Tile, Village, Building, BuildQueue, Troop, TrainingQueue, Movement, Event, Report. Table names (__tablename__): worlds, players, bot_profiles, tiles, villages, buildings, build_queue, troops, training_queue, movements, events, reports. Every column name, type, nullability, default, primary key, foreign key, unique constraint and index must match the table in BUILD.md section 7 exactly: timestamps = DateTime(timezone=True), resources = Float (DOUBLE PRECISION, use sqlalchemy.Double), JSON = JSONB (sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.JSONB), BIGSERIAL ids = BigInteger primary key with autoincrement. Use server_default for 'running', 'pending', 'moving', 0, 1.0, 100, false, '{}'::jsonb so that the alembic migration (written separately by hand) matches. Foreign keys: every *_id column listed as FK points to the right table's id (villages.player_id -> players.id, troops.home_village_id/location_village_id -> villages.id, movements.from_village_id -> villages.id, etc.). Columns described as 'BIGINT NULL' without FK (players.capital_village_id, tiles.oasis_owner_village_id, movements.to_village_id, build_queue.event_id, worlds.winner_player_id) are plain nullable BigInteger WITHOUT ForeignKey. Extra indexes from the spec: events(world_id,status,due_at), reports(player_id, created_at DESC), movements(to_village_id,status), movements(from_village_id,status), troops(location_village_id), troops(home_village_id), bot_profiles(next_think_at). realm/db/session.py must follow the snippet in the spec exactly: `engine = create_engine(settings.database_url, pool_pre_ping=True)`, `SessionLocal = sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)`, and a `session_scope()` context manager that commits on success and rolls back on exception, always closes. Import `settings` from realm.settings (module-level instance).
notes:
- Name the explicit indexes with Index('ix_<table>_<cols>', ...) in __table_args__ so the migration can use the same names.
- Index on reports uses sqlalchemy desc(): Index('ix_reports_player_id_created_at', 'player_id', desc('created_at')) -> pass the column objects/strings as SQLAlchemy supports.
- Add no extra columns, no relationships, no helper methods.
- Do NOT run the DB; the test_cmd only imports the models and prints table names.
